clue.text: Acclamation bringing share of trouble to RM Robin

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marine, and a Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine
Robin Goodfellow is the mischievous sprite of English folklore, also called Puck

explanation.surface: Someone is cheered on for sharing the trouble of a Royal Marine called Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns SHAREOF into FORHESA. A Jolly is navy slang for a Royal Marine; Robin Goodfellow is Puck of A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The song is the traditional sung tribute to someone being celebrated, a form of acclamation.

clue.text: Is half the field illegally positioned?

definitions.meaning: in cricket the field is split into the off and leg sides, so one is half of it
in football or rugby a player ahead of play in breach of the rules

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone standing in half the pitch is out of position.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket divides the field into the off side and the leg side, either side of the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketing term names one side of the pitch, and the football term means a player is beyond the permitted line.

clue.text: Coming in with a steady speed

indicators.note: the letters come in, that is sit inside, the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone arrives moving at an even, unhurried pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming in' signals letters sitting inside 'witH A STEady'. The surface's steady pace is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is speed or hurry in doing something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Roman lady was ignorant when in poverty

indicators.note: the lady sits in want, the word for poverty, whose letters wrap round her in the clue's two words

explanation.surface: An Italian woman was uneducated because she grew up poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The lady is hidden in 'was ignorant', and the letters round her spell WANT, so 'when in poverty' tells you how she sits there.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, so a lady of Rome.

clue.text: Forbidding champion to moo, say

definitions.note: moo said aloud gives moue, a pout

parts.note: a forbidding look is grim and stern
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A stern champion is told to low like a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by sound: 'moo, say' is a moue, the pouting face the French make. The cow is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A moue is a pout of the lips, a kind of wry facial expression.

clue.text: Don't accept one who whistles two notes

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle, and ref is his short name
ut is the old name for the note doh
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to go along with a person who whistles a couple of notes.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the old sol-fa name for doh, the first note of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute is to reject or deny a claim, to refuse to accept it.

clue.text: Far from the first time a below par setter has been admitted

indicators.note: the poorly setter has been let in, so placed inside the word for a span of time

parts.note: a month is a period of time
feeling below par is feeling ill
the crossword setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: It is a long time since an unwell setter was taken into hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a below par setter' is the setter feeling ill, ILL I; the crossword setter calls himself I.
explanation.definitionFit: The millionth in a sequence comes so late that it is a very long way from the first.

clue.text: Rig to fool men?

parts.note: a clot is a fool or idiot
he's are males, so men

explanation.surface: A question of whether a trick is meant to fool men.
explanation.walkthrough: HES treats 'he' as a noun, as in 'he's and she's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rig is informal for an outfit or dress, what someone is wearing.

clue.text: See 17
See 16
See 1
Religious musician who wrote plays

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, so religious
the emperor Nero was said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A devout musician who also wrote for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Wing Pinero was a late Victorian dramatist, author of The Magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Wing Pinero was an English playwright, so a dramatist who wrote plays.

clue.text: Unqualified in wrong corollary

parts.note: if being in is wrong then it follows that the opposite, being out, is correct

explanation.surface: Something is absolutely wrong as a consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The corollary of 'in' being wrong is its opposite being correct; that phrase read as one word means complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means complete or absolute, without any qualification or reservation.

clue.text: Figure of speech had Sidney bewildered

indicators.note: bewildered means confused, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone called Sidney was confused by a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bewildered' rearranges HADSIDNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hendiadys is a rhetorical figure expressing one idea by two words joined by and, such as nice and warm.

clue.text: Clear churchman's joke for an audience

indicators.note: something put on for an audience is heard, so the words are pronounced

parts.note: a deacon is a churchman and a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A clergyman's amusing remark is cleaned up for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for an audience' signals the sound: DEACON'S JEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To decongest is to relieve congestion, to clear a blocked passage.

clue.text: 1 25 11 unanimous, you old ass, as flan is cooked

indicators.note: food that is cooked is changed in form, and so these letters are

explanation.surface: Everyone sings the tribute together while someone calls a friend an old fool for baking a flan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cooked' rearranges YOUOLDASSASFLAN. The definition is the song of 1 Across sung by all.
explanation.definitionFit: The chorus that follows the song at a celebration, everyone affirming the tribute together.

clue.text: 1 25 11 incontrovertible, magazine diarist having sweets at hand, reportedly

parts.note: Which? is the British consumer magazine
The Diary of a Nobody is a comic novel told through Mr Pooter's diary

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the words are pronounced

parts.note: candy is sweets and nigh means at hand or near

explanation.surface: A magazine diarist with sweets nearby is undeniable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' signals that CANDY NIGH (sweets at hand) is said aloud. Which? is a British consumer-testing magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the line in the song asserting the tribute cannot be disputed.

clue.text: Support for bowlers, perhaps, one pursuing the hard way

indicators.note: one pursuing another follows behind it

parts.note: H stands for hard, as on pencils
a means one
a track is a way or path

explanation.surface: Cricket bowlers, one taking the difficult route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' puts A after H. Bowlers are hats here, not cricketers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat rack is a stand on which hats such as bowlers are hung.

clue.text: Not the genuine Robin? That's a bit of a relief

definitions.meaning: a false Robin Hood, an imposter of the outlaw

definitions.text: That's a bit of a relief
definitions.meaning: a lie, a synonym, is a small piece of the word relief

explanation.surface: A fake outlaw turns up, and that comes as some comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: LIE sits inside reLIEf, so a lie is a bit of a relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is an untruth, and Robin Hood made false is a fake Hood.

clue.text: Our lads afflicted with sweating

indicators.note: afflicted means troubled, so these letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: The boys are suffering from a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afflicted with' rearranges OURLADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoral is the medical adjective for perspiration, as in sudoral glands.

clue.text: Honour about half a dozen at counter

indicators.note: about means around, so the honour goes round the rest

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A decorated person stands near six at a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The counter is a verb, to prevent, not a shop fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate a difficulty is to prevent or forestall it, so to counter it.

clue.text: See 16
Person that's 'oly and tough going to flag?

parts.note: a holy person is a saint, abbreviated ST
'ard is hard with the H dropped, matching the dropped H in 'oly

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks about someone holy and hard going to fade.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''oly' tells you to drop the H of 'hard' too. Flag is a noun, a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner carried as an emblem.

clue.text: A lesser figure in Jude the Obscure — have you read this somewhere before?

definitions.text: have you read this somewhere before?

indicators.note: obscure means unclear, so these letters are hidden in a scrambled order

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals, a smaller figure than X

explanation.surface: A minor character appears in Hardy's novel Jude the Obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Obscure' rearranges A, V and JUDE. The novel title is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the uncanny feeling of having experienced something before.

clue.text: See 1
Film brothers keeping a horse that brings in money

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the film company holds the rest

parts.note: Warner Brothers is the Hollywood film studio
gee, or gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: Hollywood brothers own a horse that wins them money.
explanation.walkthrough: Warner Bros is a Hollywood studio founded by four brothers; GEE is a nursery word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage earner is a person whose work brings in money as pay.

clue.text: Lounge used for thinking

definitions.meaning: to lounge is to idle or laze about
the head, as in use your ..., rhyming slang ... of bread

explanation.surface: Lazing around is good for reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' means think; loaf of bread is Cockney rhyming slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to idle, and the slang word for the head is the part you think with.

clue.text: Unpredictable after opening of safety pin

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: kittle is a Scots word for unpredictable or capricious

explanation.surface: A safety pin springs open without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: KITTLE is Scots for tricky or unpredictable. The pin is a skittle, not a safety pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A skittle is one of the wooden pins knocked down in the game of skittles.

clue.text: Invert what 12 did to restrict children

indicators.note: to invert is to turn upside down, here swapping the two halves of the phrase

parts.note: Pinero, the answer at 12, penned plays: pen play

explanation.surface: Turning a playwright's craft round to keep the kids in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invert' swaps PEN and PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is an enclosure that keeps a small child confined while playing.
